answer: An agent economy can require every identity to escrow a scarce bond before its votes or reputation count. If coordinated fake accounts manipulate rewards, the protocol detects their shared behavior and slashes the bonds, compensating those harmed. This cannot prevent copying identities; it makes each one costly to operate. A quill-marked claim must cross a canyon of scrutiny, so an oasis of easy rewards comes at the risk of losing real capital for every sybil.
